title: Streaming attention kernel rewrite: rotary-anchor normalization + cooperative KV prefetch
author: Harper Li
description: Motivation: Streaming workloads with heterogeneous sequence-lengths suffer from rotary phase misalignment and non-optimal KV prefetch timing, which increases tail latency under continuous batching. This PR rewrites the attention hot path to introduce a rotary-anchor normalization stage and a cooperative KV prefetch/eviction heuristic designed for continuous batching and mixed request sizes. Summary of changes: 1) rotary-anchor normalization: introduce a lightweight per-request anchor adjustment that normalizes rotary phase across concatenated prefix sequences to avoid rotational drift when merging KV caches from different segments; implemented in runtimes/attn/rotary_anchor.h and applied in the attn forward path. 2) streaming-aware attention kernel: refactor the streaming kernel to expose an anchor parameter so fused rotary math executes deterministically when batch composition changes mid-ephemeral; new kernel is in runtimes/attn/streaming_kernel.cu with a fallback scalar path for small heads. 3) cooperative KV prefetch scheduler: a scheduler that tags streaming requests with prefetch urgency and coordinates across worker threads to avoid redundant KV loads and reduce memory churn; implemented in runtimes/kv/prefetch_scheduler.py and integrated with the runtime dispatcher. 4) eviction heuristic: lightweight probabilistic LRU tuned for continuous-batching patterns to free stale KV entries quickly without perturbing hot prefixes. 5) tests and benchmarks: added microbenchmarks and an end-to-end canary script under tests/perf/benchmark_streaming_rotary.py and stress tests in tests/ci/streaming_kv_stress.yaml. Performance: on our internal canary cluster (p4d-like), steady-state throughput improves by 8-14% for mixed-length GPT-like models with a 12-18% reduction in 95th percentile latency under continuous batching workload. Memory overhead for rotary-anchor normalization is ~0.5-1.2% of KV cache size depending on batch composition. Compatibility and fallback: the new kernel registers a capability flag; older deployment images will continue to use the previous kernel. We included a safe toggle in runtime config (runtime.attn.enable_rotary_anchor) and a canary rollout plan. Rollout plan: canary on Dedicated pool 'canary-rotary' for 48 hours, monitor token-level latency, kv cache hit ratio, and regression alerts. If all checks pass promote to 20% traffic then gradually to 100%. Related work: follows up on ENG-4321 (continuous-batching improvements) and complements earlier flash/kernels work but differs by focusing on cross-request rotary phase consistency and cooperative KV prefetch timing rather than kernel-level attention tiling. Testing: unit tests added for rotary-anchor math, multi-segment KV reconciliation, and eviction policy; perf harness includes synthetic and sampled production traces. Security and safety: no new network surfaces; prefetch scheduler runs inside existing runtime process. Release notes: Added streaming-attention rotary anchor normalization and cooperative KV prefetch scheduler; improves throughput and tail latency for mixed-length streaming workloads. TODOs and follow-ups: 1) extend anchor normalization to support rotary variants with per-head biases (ENG-4389), 2) port the prefetch scheduler to C++ worker for lower overhead in high-concurrency environments, 3) add quantized kernel tests for fp8/fp16 runtimes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and microbenchmarks attached - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary plan documented - [x] Perf numbers validated on canary cluster - [x] Backwards compatibility toggle included

review_comments: Lucas Nguyen: The rotary math looks sound but please add a small benchmark that measures per-head overhead when anchor normalization is enabled vs disabled.

Priya Patel: Can we get a quick check on GPU memory pressure with the new prefetch heuristic on 8xA100? Concerned about bursty traffic.
Harper Li: Ran a 24h stress with 8xA100 canary cluster; attached logs to the Linear ticket; memory median unchanged, peak reduced in 70% of runs.
Marco Alvarez: Nit: prefer C++ scheduler for lower GIL overhead in high-concurrency runs; ok to iterate after merge.

review_summary: Three reviewers, iterative feedback focused on perf coverage and memory behaviour. One CI run failed initially due to a flaky unit in attention tiler; flake fixed and all checks green. Review approvals: Lucas Nguyen APPROVED, Priya Patel APPROVED after additional memory stress data, Marco Alvarez APPROVED with a follow-up request for C++ port. Merged via squash after green CI.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about core tiling changes; it instead adds a deterministic normalization layer and a scheduler that cooperates with existing batching. Operators: runtime.attn.enable_rotary_anchor=false by default until canary is promoted. Monitoring dashboards created: dashboard/perf/rotary-anchor-canary and alerts under infra/alerts/rotary_anchor_regression.alert
short_description: Introduce rotary-anchor normalization and cooperative KV prefetch to reduce tail latency for streaming mixed-length workloads
